newsitem.title: RUSSIA: U.S., Russia report progress in NATO talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Russia report progress in NATO talks.

text.p: Russia and the United States said on Thursday that they had made progress in narrowing their differences over NATO expansion plans but that differences remained.

"We may have somewhat narrowed the differences," U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright told reporters after talks in Moscow with Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov. "We still have some way to go," she added. Primakov took a similiar line: "Our talks I believe were successful and they will be continued," he said.
Primakov and Albright were discussing ways to soothe Russia's unease about NATO's plans to invite some former Warsaw Pact members in July to join the alliance.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who wants Moscow to have a say in NATO affairs and is seeking a commitment from the alliance not to move its infrastructure on to the territory of new members, has said he wants to sign a deal governing relations with NATO on May 27.
"Our goal today was not to get it done but to make sure we got it done right," Albright said.

Primakov said the two sides were still divided by military questions, without elaborating. "There are some outstanding issues...these include mainly military questions," he said. During the talks Yeltsin had spoken to Albright by telephone for at least 40 minutes, Primakov added.
